summary: South Africa admits most Western passports visa-free — 90 days for the US, UK, most of Western Europe, Japan, Brazil and Russia, and 30 days for several others — while nationalities such as China and India need a visa, which they can now also get online through the Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) for arrival at four international airports. Home Affairs requires at least one blank passport page for endorsements.

fee.notes: Home Affairs issues the eVisa as a port of entry visa (Immigration Act s.10); its tariff list (Government Gazette 55209, 17 August 2026) charges R425 for it, the same as a visitor’s visa. Home Affairs’ published turnaround time for an eVisa is 10 working days. The eVisa has been rolled out gradually to selected nationalities, so confirm on the Home Affairs website that it is open to yours.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 30 days after your intended departure from South Africa — though at least 6 months' validity is recommended, since airlines and neighboring countries often apply stricter standards.

source.name: Department of Home Affairs — Types of Visas
Department of Home Affairs — Types of Visas

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required if your journey starts in, or passes through, the yellow fever belt of Africa or South America. Only direct transit through such a country is exempt, so check your routing if it connects through an African hub such as Nairobi or Addis Ababa.

source.name: South African Department of Home Affairs — Types of Visas (requirements for entering South Africa)

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but medical coverage is strongly recommended — South Africa's excellent private hospitals require payment guarantees, and public hospitals are under strain.

source.name: South African Department of Home Affairs — Types of Visas (requirements for entering South Africa)

onwardTicket.text: Visitors must be able to show a return or onward ticket; airlines check this at check-in and immigration officers may ask again on arrival.

source.name: Department of Home Affairs — Types of Visas

proofOfFunds.text: Visitors must have sufficient funds for their stay; there is no published fixed amount, but immigration officers can ask for bank statements or cash and cards as evidence.

source.name: Department of Home Affairs — Types of Visas

declarations.name: SARS online traveller declaration
declarations.submitWindow: Before you travel, for entry and for departure
declarations.text: From 1 July 2026 every traveller entering or leaving South Africa by air, land or sea must submit a customs traveller declaration online before travelling, unless a limited paper-based exception applies. Submit it on the SARS website, the SATMS app or the SARS MobiApp, one per traveller including children, and keep the emailed confirmation to show customs officers.

source.name: South African Revenue Service — Customs Online Traveller Declaration

currencyLimits.text: Carrying more than R100,000 in South African banknotes, or foreign currency worth more than R100,000, into or out of South Africa needs written permission from the South African Reserve Bank; customs can seize the excess. Declaring the cash you carry is voluntary, on the online traveller declaration or the paper form TD-01. The rand-note limit does not apply to travel within the Common Monetary Area.

source.name: South African Revenue Service — Travellers (excess currency)

conflict.name: UK Foreign Office — South Africa entry requirements

notes: Children under 18 should travel with an unabridged (full) birth certificate; the rules for foreign minors were relaxed in 2019 but officials still recommend carrying one, and it remains required in some cases (e.g. A child traveling with one parent or unaccompanied).

The South African Revenue Service allows each traveller to bring in duty-free no more than 200 cigarettes and 20 cigars, 250 g of tobacco, 2 litres of wine and 1 litre in total of other alcoholic beverages; under-18s get no alcohol or tobacco allowance.

payments.text: No official source we read describes card acceptance in South Africa. The UK FCDO warns that card skimming is widespread and advises changing large sums only in banks or secure shopping malls.

safety.text: South Africa has high crime rates, but millions of tourists visit safely each year by managing risk: use Uber/Bolt or hotel transfers rather than walking at night, keep valuables out of sight, keep car doors locked and windows up in cities (smash-and-grab and carjacking occur at intersections), and stick to well-traveled areas. Ask locals which neighbourhoods to avoid.

tips.text: The Department of Home Affairs requires at least one blank page in your passport for entry and departure endorsements; UK travel advice asks for two. Check your passport before booking.

Traveling with children? Carry each child's unabridged (full) birth certificate and, if one parent is absent, a consent affidavit. The strict 2015-era rules were relaxed for foreign tourists, but officials still ask in edge cases.

If you drive, the Government of Canada says traffic drives on the left, advises driving defensively and avoiding travel after dark, and recommends a rental company with a 24-hour emergency service. Keep doors locked and valuables out of sight.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for South Africa?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders get a free visitor's permit on arrival for stays of up to 90 days. You do need a passport valid for 30 days beyond departure with at least one blank page, and a return or onward ticket.

faq.question: How many blank passport pages does South Africa require?
faq.answer: At least one blank page for entry and departure endorsements, according to the Department of Home Affairs; UK travel advice says two. If you are short on pages, renew your passport before the trip.

faq.question: What documents do children need to enter South Africa?
faq.answer: Foreign visa-exempt minors no longer must present a birth certificate since the 2019 relaxation, but Home Affairs still recommends carrying the child's unabridged birth certificate, and it is required in specific cases. A child traveling with one parent should also carry consent from the other. Check the Department of Home Affairs guidance before flying with kids.

faq.question: Do Chinese and Indian citizens need a visa for South Africa?
faq.answer: Yes. Both need a visa. Since South Africa's G20 Presidency, travellers from China, India, Indonesia and Mexico can apply online for an Electronic Travel Authorisation at eta.dha.gov.za, officially launched on 12 August 2026; outcomes typically arrive within 24 hours, and it currently covers arrivals at OR Tambo, Cape Town, King Shaka and Lanseria airports only. The ETA is not yet compulsory: you can still apply through a South African mission or its visa contractor, or through the eVisa where it is available.

faq.question: Is South Africa safe for tourists?
faq.answer: Crime is a real risk. The UK FCDO reports violent attacks on hikers in Table Mountain National Park, widespread card skimming, and violence linked to tensions between e-hailing and metered taxi drivers. The Government of Canada says travel on foot is inadvisable in most areas and advises avoiding travel after dark. Get local advice on areas to avoid and check your government’s current advice.
